policy: Build or deploy a new behavior only when its stated outcome has a measurable benefit over a recorded baseline.

entries.hypothesis: The upstream R2 default-processor heading control path may produce observed forward displacement, unlike the completed secondary-processor heading attempt.

baseline.summary: The secondary-processor/tripod path completed safely with no observed locomotion.

measurement.collection: Supervising operator observes direction, displacement, and final stance after one bounded pulse.

entries.decision_rule: A positive observed displacement establishes only a candidate drive path for further calibrated stop testing; no displacement closes this stock-heading variation without retry.
entries.result: Two separately authorized default-primary heading pulses completed with the watchdog safe hold, and the supervising operator confirmed locomotion.
entries.next_action: Measure one conservative, bounded calibration segment and its stopped final state before claiming distance, speed, or physical-stop effectiveness.

entries.hypothesis: The verified stock/default-primary heading path can produce one conservatively bounded forward segment that an operator can measure, establishing a calibration baseline without exceeding the Phase 1 0.25 m limit.

baseline.summary: The stock/default-primary heading diagnostic produced operator-observed locomotion, but the distance and stopping effectiveness remain unmeasured.

measurement.collection: A supervising operator measures the forward displacement from fixed start and finish marks, observes direction, final stance, and stationary state after the independent watchdog safe hold.

entries.decision_rule: A measured segment within the 0.25 m bound establishes only a preliminary motion calibration datum; unexpected direction, excessive distance, or any abnormal behavior stops the branch and leaves physical-stop effectiveness unverified.
entries.next_action: Review and stage a distinct, fixed-bounds calibration runner, then require fresh exact motion authorization and preflight before one HIL run.

entries.hypothesis: Selecting the R2 secondary processor and explicit tripod stance will produce observed forward wheel motion where earlier primary/default-path attempts did not.

baseline.summary: Four prior bounded forward pulses and one R2 generic-drive attempt produced no observed locomotion.

measurement.collection: Supervising operator observes direction and measured displacement after the single bounded pulse.

entries.result: LEDs and the three-leg to two-leg stance cycle were observed; no locomotion was observed.
entries.decision_rule: No observed displacement means this path is not a validated wheel-control path and must not be retried unchanged.
entries.next_action: Compare the exact encoded stock high-level control path with the reviewed diagnostic packet path without accessing hardware.

entries.hypothesis: A static, byte-level comparison can identify a control-path difference between the current diagnostic and the upstream recommended high-level R2 path, producing a distinct testable hypothesis before any new hardware action.

baseline.summary: Current secondary-processor diagnostic completes safely but produces no observed locomotion.

measurement.collection: Deterministic static comparison of reviewed upstream/library source and locally encoded test fixtures; no BLE import, scan, connection, or write.

entries.decision_rule: Build a new diagnostic only if the comparison finds at least one reviewed, R2-applicable difference and a simulation test captures it; otherwise close the locomotion branch pending new external evidence.
entries.result: The pinned upstream R2 binding retains proc=None for stock raw-motor and heading calls, while the completed diagnostic explicitly used Processors.SECONDARY; deterministic audit found two control-path differences without hardware access.
entries.next_action: Do not schedule another HIL run until a distinct, documented hypothesis explains why the stock primary/default control path would improve on its prior no-motion result.
